evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — add an Order entity with draft and submitted states. Order has orderId, customer and amount.
evals.expected_output: Checks the connection with cyoda-status.sh, lists models with cyoda-call.sh GET /model/ (empty), reads cyoda help models LIFECYCLE/ENDPOINTS and workflows WORKFLOW SCHEMA, reads the schema version from cyoda-help.sh workflows schema-version versions at run time, asks for unique keys and the changeLevel, shows the three files for confirmation, writes order-v1-sample.json / order-v1-workflow.json / order-v1-config.json in the TypeScript default dirs plus cyoda-manifest.json at the project root, then registers in the canonical order (import sample, unique keys if any, lock, changeLevel if any, import workflow) through cyoda-call.sh, re-lists the models and ends with 'next, type /cyoda:test'.

files._simulated/instance.md: cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 VERSION=0.8.4. GET /model/ returns []. Every POST/PUT returns 200. The developer answers: no unique keys; changeLevel none (strict).

assertions.text: Names the help path and section it reads for the facts, at least `cyoda-help.sh models --section LIFECYCLE` (or ENDPOINTS) before registering and `cyoda-help.sh workflows --section "WORKFLOW SCHEMA"` (or TRANSITIONS) before generating the workflow
Reads the workflow schema version at run time from `workflows schema-version versions` (`.current`) and does not hard-code a version such as "1" or "1.4" from memory

Registers in this order: POST /model/import/JSON/SAMPLE_DATA/order/1, then PUT /model/order/1/lock, then the workflow import POST /model/order/1/workflow/import — and creates no entity before the workflow is imported
Every API call goes through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-call.sh`; no raw curl with a hand-built auth header
Asks which changeLevel the developer wants and records the answer (null here) in order-v1-config.json
Writes order-v1-sample.json, order-v1-workflow.json and order-v1-config.json in the TypeScript default dirs (src/data/, src/workflows/, src/config/)
Creates cyoda-manifest.json at the project root with manifestVersion 1 and an entry {name: order, modelVersion: 1, sample, workflow, config} whose paths are relative to the project root
Shows the generated files and waits for the developer's yes before registering
Does not say the schema stays unlocked or in a 'discover mode'; the model is locked before the workflow import
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke or run another skill itself

evals.prompt: /cyoda:build — RiskAssessment needs an `approved` state reached when a function criterion on our scoring node passes; if the node keeps timing out, does the transition fail or retry?
evals.expected_output: Lists models (riskassessment v1 LOCKED) and reads the project's riskassessment-v1-workflow.json. Reads `workflows` CRITERIA and PROCESSORS itself (and the function condition shape in `search`, or `errors DISPATCH_TIMEOUT`). Says what help states, naming the sections (a `function` criterion is dispatched to a compute member and must be the whole criterion; its `responseTimeoutMs` defaults to 30000; a dispatch that times out is DISPATCH_TIMEOUT, a retryable 503; the cyoda-go dispatcher is single-shot, so the engine does not retry) and that help doesn't settle how a timed-out criterion on an automated transition plays out, then asks whether to spike it on a throwaway cyoda-go (in-memory with mock auth, or the stack in Docker). The developer says no, so it starts nothing and carries on from help: adds `approved` and an automated submitted → approved transition whose criterion is the whole `function` criterion (name risk-score-passes, calculationNodesTags scoring), edits riskassessment-v1-workflow.json in place (same model version, no sample re-import), shows it, and after the developer's yes re-imports the workflow via cyoda-call.sh POST /model/riskassessment/1/workflow/import, then hands off with 'next, type /cyoda:test'.

files._simulated/developer.md: riskassessment v1 is registered and LOCKED on the project's local cyoda-go, with no entities yet. `approved` is reached automatically from `submitted` when the function criterion `risk-score-passes` on their compute node tagged `scoring` passes; `approved` is terminal; nothing else changes. If offered any extra experiment or check, the developer declines: "No, just build it from the docs." Shown the changed workflow, the developer says: "yes".

assertions.text: Reads the `workflows` CRITERIA and PROCESSORS sections itself (cyoda-help.sh or `cyoda help`) before answering or generating the workflow, and names the sections it used in its reply
Before registering anything, asks whether to spike the timeout behaviour on a throwaway cyoda-go (in-memory with mock auth, or the stack in Docker), because help doesn't settle it
After the developer says no, starts no cyoda-go process or container; every instance call goes to the project's own instance through cyoda-call.sh

Answers the timeout question from what help states (e.g. a criterion dispatch that exceeds `responseTimeoutMs` fails with DISPATCH_TIMEOUT, a retryable 503; the cyoda-go dispatcher is single-shot, so the engine does not retry and a retry is the caller's) and names what help leaves open (e.g. whether the triggering write fails or the transition counts as not matched, leaving the entity in `submitted`) instead of presenting it as settled; an inference marked as such is fine

Proceeds with the increment: adds `approved` and an automated (`manual: false`) submitted → approved transition whose criterion is the whole `function` criterion (`type: function`, `function.name` risk-score-passes, `function.config.calculationNodesTags` scoring), not nested in a `group`
Edits src/workflows/riskassessment-v1-workflow.json in place and keeps model version 1: no new model version, no unlock, no sample re-import; the manifest entry is unchanged

After the developer's yes, re-imports with cyoda-call.sh POST /model/riskassessment/1/workflow/import with the schema version substituted from `workflows schema-version versions`, and the real response in the transcript is a success
The hand-off says 'next, type `/cyoda:test`' and does not say it will invoke another skill
